Nice and deep rail for the CF card. Excellent product. I get about 35mb/sec transfer times with my Transcend 400x 64GB CF card using USB 2.0.

The biggest culprit with most CF card readers is that the rails that align the CF card to the pins (rails on the side of the CF card) are not deep enough. When you insert a CF card to a reader with shallow rails, it can be easy to bend the pins.

The Transcend P8 has very deep rails for the CF card reader, so a large majority of the CF card sinks into the reader before contacting the pins. This way you can be assured that the pins are aligned correctly without error for bending the pins.

Anyway, great product!

For eSATA, don't make mistake!. Wouldn't recognize on the eSATA port. It would detect the HDD, but would not format nor store data. I thought it would be plug and play. I submitted a return request (which the seller approved), but after extensive Googling, discovered how to make it work on my machine.

1) For Windows 7 (I think Windows 10 may not have this issue), make sure you have the registry entry to allow AHCI.
2) In BIOS, make sure your boot devices are in proper order.
3) In BIOS, update RAID configuration to AHCI.

After that, it is operating as expected.
